fact: Lady Mary Wortley Montagu promoted smallpox inoculation in Britain in 1721, decades before Jenner’s cowpox vaccine.
nfact: Katherine Johnson checked the orbit calculations for John Glenn’s 1962 flight. He asked for her by name.

fact: Skin is the body’s largest organ.
nfact: Lightning is about five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.

fact: Your heart beats roughly 100,000 times a day.
nfact: Cathy Freeman lit the cauldron at the Sydney 2000 Olympics, then won 400 m gold ten days later.

fact: The first X-ray of a human body part, in 1895, was of Anna Bertha Röntgen’s hand, wedding ring and all.
nfact: Sharks are older than trees, by tens of millions of years.

fact: The average age of menopause in Australia is around 51.
nfact: A day on Venus is longer than its year.

fact: Elizabeth Blackwell became the first woman to earn a medical degree in the United States, in 1849.
nfact: Scotland’s national animal is the unicorn.

fact: Marie Curie, born on 7 November 1867, is still the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences: physics (1903) and chemistry (1911).
nfact: Apples float because roughly a quarter of their volume is air.

fact: The first CT scan of a patient was done in London on 1 October 1971, on a woman with a suspected brain tumour.
nfact: Wilma Rudolph wore a leg brace as a child after polio, then won three sprint golds at the 1960 Olympics.

fact: The medical name for hiccups is singultus.
nfact: Paralympian Kurt Fearnley crawled the 96 km Kokoda Track in 2009.

fact: Mary Seacole, a Jamaican-born nurse, ran the ‘British Hotel’ near Balaclava, feeding and nursing soldiers in the Crimean War.
nfact: Bubble wrap was first invented in 1957 as a textured wallpaper.

fact: Florence Nightingale used a ‘rose diagram’ to show that most Crimean War soldiers died of preventable disease, not wounds.
nfact: Neville Bonner became the first Aboriginal member of Australia’s federal parliament in 1971.

fact: WHO says pneumonia is the single largest infectious cause of death in children worldwide. Vaccines, clean air and good nutrition all cut the risk.
nfact: Mary Anning helped uncover one of the first ichthyosaur fossils in 1811, when she was about 12.

fact: Susan La Flesche Picotte became the first Native American woman to earn a medical degree in the US, in 1889.
nfact: Owls can’t move their eyes, so they turn their heads, up to about 270 degrees.

fact: Dorothy Hodgkin worked out the structures of penicillin, vitamin B12 and insulin. She won the 1964 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
nfact: Ash Barty, a Ngarigo woman, won Wimbledon in 2021.

fact: René Laennec invented the stethoscope in 1816: a rolled-up tube of paper, so he didn’t have to put his ear to a patient’s chest.
nfact: The dot over a lowercase i or j is called a tittle.

fact: Cells taken from Henrietta Lacks in 1951, without her consent, became HeLa: the first human cell line to grow indefinitely.
nfact: The shortest war on record, between Britain and Zanzibar in 1896, lasted under an hour.

fact: Australia began a national school HPV vaccination program in 2007, using a vaccine built on work by Ian Frazer and Jian Zhou in Brisbane.
nfact: The ‘seeds’ on a strawberry are actually tiny fruits, each with a seed inside.

fact: In his 1945 Nobel lecture, Alexander Fleming warned that underdosing penicillin could breed resistant bacteria.
nfact: Flamingos are pink because of pigments in the algae and shrimp they eat.

fact: Dr Māui Pōmare, the first Māori doctor, qualified in 1899 and led public health work in Māori communities.
nfact: Earth’s days are getting very slightly longer over time, as the Moon’s tides slow its spin.

fact: Nettie Stevens discovered in 1905 that X and Y chromosomes determine sex.
nfact: The Eiffel Tower can grow around 15 cm taller in summer as the iron expands.

fact: Professor Fiona Wood co-invented spray-on skin for burns and was named Australian of the Year in 2005.
nfact: Honey can keep for decades, even centuries, because it’s low in water and quite acidic.

fact: The Paralympic movement grew from the Stoke Mandeville Games, organised by Dr Ludwig Guttmann in 1948.
nfact: Frida Kahlo painted many works from her bed, using an easel built to fit over it.

fact: Japanese chemist Jokichi Takamine isolated adrenaline in 1901, one of the first hormones ever purified.
nfact: You can’t see the Great Wall of China from the Moon with the naked eye.

fact: Louis Braille, blind from the age of three, published his raised-dot reading system in 1829.
nfact: Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood.

fact: In 1943 Mary Hunt found a mouldy cantaloupe in a Peoria market. Its strain of mould made far more penicillin and helped mass production.
nfact: Louise Sauvage won the Boston Marathon wheelchair race four times.

fact: Tu Youyou found artemisinin, a key malaria drug, after reading a 1,600-year-old Chinese remedy. She won the 2015 Nobel Prize in Medicine.
nfact: Sudoku began as ‘Number Place’ in a US puzzle magazine in 1979. Japan’s Nikoli named it Sudoku in 1984.

fact: Oral rehydration solution, refined in Bangladesh and India, is a simple mix of salts and sugar that has saved millions of lives from diarrhoea.
nfact: Marie Curie is the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences: physics and chemistry.

fact: The World Health Organization declared smallpox eradicated in 1980, the first human disease wiped out.
nfact: Wombats produce cube-shaped poo.

fact: In 1847 Ignaz Semmelweis showed that handwashing with chlorinated lime cut deaths from childbed fever.
nfact: Beethoven wrote his Ninth Symphony while almost completely deaf.

fact: Adults have about 206 bones. Babies start with around 300, and many fuse as they grow.
nfact: Alan Turing, the code-breaker and computing pioneer, proposed his famous Turing test in 1950.
